atoms.text: This guide configures the role that the DurableSync replication service assumes to copy new objects from a source bucket to the disaster recovery bucket dr-orders-replica. The destination bucket and the role replication-writer both belong to account 111122223333. Create the role with a trust policy that lets the DurableSync service principal assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:ListBucket on the destination bucket and s3:PutObject on arn:cloud:s3:::dr-orders-replica/*. Do not change the bucket policy of dr-orders-replica, because the role's identity-based policy alone carries the grant when the bucket and role share an account. Check that the existing bucket policy contains no explicit Deny statement that matches the role. Start a replication job for the prefix orders/ and confirm that new objects appear in the destination bucket with matching ETags. A write that fails with AccessDenied in the job event log means an action is missing from the role's identity-based policy.

This guide configures the role that the DurableSync replication service assumes to copy new objects from a source bucket to the disaster recovery bucket dr-orders-replica. The destination bucket is owned by account 444455556666, while the role replication-writer belongs to account 111122223333. Create the role in account 111122223333 with a trust policy that lets the DurableSync service principal assume it. In account 444455556666, the bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement that names arn:cloud:iam::111122223333:role/replication-writer as the principal. That statement allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket and s3:PutObject on arn:cloud:s3:::dr-orders-replica/*. The bucket policy carries the grant, so the role needs no extra permissions from the owner's account. Start a replication job for the prefix orders/ and confirm that new objects appear in the destination bucket with matching ETags. A write that fails with AccessDenied in the job event log means the principal ARN or an action is missing from the bucket policy statement.

This guide covers granting a nightly database backup agent permission to upload dump files to the bucket db-backups-prod. The agent runs under the role backup-uploader, and both the role and the bucket are in account 111122223333. The agent writes compressed dumps to the prefix postgres/daily/ and never reads them back. Attach an identity-based policy to backup-uploader that allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:cloud:s3:::db-backups-prod/postgres/daily/*. Add s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket itself so the agent can clean up incomplete uploads. Leave the bucket policy of db-backups-prod unchanged, because the role's identity-based policy is the only source of the grant. Run the agent once manually and verify that the dump object appears under postgres/daily/ with the expected size. If the upload is rejected, review the identity-based policy resource ARN for a missing /* suffix.

This guide describes how to let a restore service read archived backups during a recovery exercise. The restore service uses the role restore-reader, and the archive bucket cold-archive-2024 is in the same account, 111122223333. The service lists objects under the prefix snapshots/ and downloads the ones selected for restoration. Attach an identity-based policy to restore-reader that allows s3:GetObject on arn:cloud:s3:::cold-archive-2024/snapshots/*. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a condition limiting the listing prefix to snapshots/. Do not edit the bucket policy, because the identity-based policy provides the whole grant within a single account. Run a test restore of one snapshot and compare its checksum with the value recorded at backup time. Any AccessDenied response on a listing call usually means the prefix condition does not match the prefix in the request.

This guide explains the permissions needed to replicate object versions and delete markers from a versioned bucket to its backup counterpart. The replication role version-replicator, the source bucket media-primary, and the destination bucket media-backup are all in account 111122223333. The role reads versions from the source and writes them to the destination with their original version metadata. Attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObjectVersion and s3:GetObjectVersionTagging on the source bucket objects. In the same policy, allow s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateDelete on arn:cloud:s3:::media-backup/*. Keep the bucket policies of both buckets unchanged, since the role's identity-based policy grants everything required. Enable versioning on both buckets before starting the job. After the first run, confirm that the version count under a sample key is identical in the two buckets.

This guide explains the permissions needed to replicate object versions and delete markers from a versioned bucket to its backup counterpart. The replication role version-replicator and the source bucket media-primary are in account 111122223333, while the destination bucket media-backup is owned by account 444455556666. The role reads versions from the source and writes them to the destination with their original version metadata. The source side is covered by the role's own account. On the destination, the bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement naming arn:cloud:iam::111122223333:role/version-replicator as the principal. That statement allows s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateDelete on arn:cloud:s3:::media-backup/*. Enable versioning on both buckets before starting the job. After the first run, confirm that the version count under a sample key is identical in the two buckets.

This guide sets up an integrity verification job that audits backup objects without modifying them. The job runs as the role integrity-auditor and examines the bucket backup-vault-east, both in account 111122223333. It lists every object under the prefix weekly/ and reads each object to recompute its checksum. Attach an identity-based policy to integrity-auditor that allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket and s3:GetObject on arn:cloud:s3:::backup-vault-east/weekly/*. Do not grant any write or delete actions, so the job stays strictly read-only. The bucket policy of backup-vault-east is not modified, because the identity-based policy alone carries the grant. Schedule the job to run after the weekly backup window closes. Review the job report for checksum mismatches, and treat any AccessDenied entry as a missing read action in the role's policy.

This guide sets up an integrity verification job that audits backup objects without modifying them. The job runs as the role integrity-auditor in account 111122223333 and examines the bucket backup-vault-east, which is owned by account 444455556666. It lists every object under the prefix weekly/ and reads each object to recompute its checksum. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement naming arn:cloud:iam::111122223333:role/integrity-auditor as the principal. The statement allows only s3:ListBucket on the bucket and s3:GetObject on arn:cloud:s3:::backup-vault-east/weekly/*. No write or delete actions are included, so the job stays strictly read-only. Schedule the job to run after the weekly backup window closes. Review the job report for checksum mismatches, and treat any AccessDenied entry as a missing read action in the bucket policy statement.

This guide configures a retention job that deletes expired backup objects from the bucket app-backups-archive. The job runs as the role retention-pruner, and the bucket is in the same account, 111122223333. It lists objects under the prefix full/ and deletes those older than 35 days. Attach an identity-based policy to retention-pruner that allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket and s3:DeleteObject on arn:cloud:s3:::app-backups-archive/full/*. Restrict deletion to the full/ prefix so that incremental backups under incr/ are never affected. Leave the bucket policy untouched, because the identity-based policy supplies the grant within one account. Run the job in dry-run mode first and compare the proposed deletion list against the retention rule. Enable real deletion only after the list matches, and check the audit log for the resulting DeleteObject events.

This guide configures a retention job that deletes expired backup objects from the bucket app-backups-archive. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement naming arn:cloud:iam::111122223333:role/retention-pruner as the principal. The statement allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket and s3:DeleteObject on arn:cloud:s3:::app-backups-archive/full/*. Deletion is restricted to the full/ prefix so that incremental backups under incr/ are never affected. Run the job in dry-run mode first and compare the proposed deletion list against the retention rule. Enable real deletion only after the list matches, and check the audit log for the resulting DeleteObject events.

This guide covers permissions for a cluster snapshot exporter that writes volume snapshots to the bucket snapshot-store. The exporter runs under the role snapshot-exporter, and the bucket is in the same account, 111122223333. Each snapshot is split into chunks and uploaded with multipart uploads to the prefix cluster-a/. Attach an identity-based policy to snapshot-exporter that allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:cloud:s3:::snapshot-store/cluster-a/*. Add a condition requiring the header x-store-storage-class to equal STANDARD_IA so that snapshots use the infrequent-access tier. The bucket policy is not changed, because the role's identity-based policy alone grants the access. Trigger an export of one small volume and inspect the resulting objects. Confirm that each chunk reports the infrequent-access storage class.

It also includes a condition requiring the header x-store-storage-class to equal STANDARD_IA so that snapshots use the infrequent-access tier. This guide explains how to let a log archival service copy rotated application logs into the bucket logs-longterm. The service uses the role log-archiver, and the bucket is in the same account, 111122223333. Logs are written under the prefix app/YYYY/MM/ and are never overwritten after upload. Attach an identity-based policy to log-archiver that allows s3:PutObject on arn:cloud:s3:::logs-longterm/app/*. Add a statement denying s3:PutObject unless the request includes the header x-store-object-lock-mode, so every archived file is locked against changes. Do not edit the bucket policy of logs-longterm, because the identity-based policy carries the full grant. Upload one rotated log file with the service's test command. Confirm that the object shows a retention lock and that a second write to the same key is rejected.

A second statement denies s3:PutObject unless the request includes the header x-store-object-lock-mode, so every archived file is locked against changes. Upload one rotated log file with the service's test command. Confirm that the object shows a retention lock and that a second write to the same key is rejected.
